correctness.rationale: With fixed classifications, any receptive initial weight furnishes a deterministic positive lower bound on the normalizer; m bounds it above. After n selections of a negative edge, its conditional hazard until the next lies between a_e δ_e^n and b_e δ_e^n, with both constants positive and finite. Taking τ_n just after draw n of this edge makes it a stopping time without an indexing ambiguity. Each wait is finite; a union bound at δ_e^{−(1−ε)n} and iterated survival at δ_e^{−(1+ε)n} give summable bounds even without independent waits. Borel–Cantelli at countably many ε then gives log wait/n→|log δ_e|, which passes to log τ_n/n by the last-summand lower bound and geometric-rate upper bound. Inversion and the exact weight identity give the two negative-edge limits. Each positive edge has uniformly positive conditional selection probability, hence positive lower frequency by the bounded martingale strong law. Its exact deficit (1−z_f(0))(1−γ_f)^{N_f(t)} tends exponentially to zero; together with the negative result this makes each positive selection probability tend to 1/k, giving the stated frequency and log-deficit rate by Cesàro and the same strong law. For eventual stabilization use a frozen coupling started at each deterministic integer T and partition, driven by the same future uniforms; the probability-one fixed-class result holds given the observed weights at T and the two trajectories agree on the event of permanent matching classes after T. A countable union avoids conditioning on a possibly anticipative last-change time. This proves the assertion only on the event stated, not stabilization itself.
residual_risks: The argument needs an eventually persistent positive class; the all-discount comparator is not part of the mixed regime. The finite simulations are not almost-sure evidence.

This is coverage by an immediate extension of the actual proof, not a claim that the indexed statement literally quantifies over heterogeneous factors.

The explicit deficit rate follows by taking logs of that identity and substituting the known frequency. There is no distinct valuable remainder to repair on these claims. value.rationale: The mixed-regime rates quantify a genuine distinction between disappearing weight and a finite selection count: inactive contacts recur infinitely often but only on a logarithmic calendar-time scale. The count coefficient distinguishes discount factors that cannot be distinguished by the universal weight exponent alone. This is value of the mathematical law, not an incremental contribution over the matching result; the per-edge generalization has no separate scientific advance in the frozen formulation.
residual_risks: No finite-window confidence bounds or general stabilization theorem follow from these asymptotics.
